evidence: Quint. 1.4.19: noster sermō articulōs nōn dēsīderat
terms.comment: English “a” is not translated: “a dog was carrying a piece of meat across a river” is canis per flūmen carnem cum ferret (Phaedr. 1.4.2).

terms.gloss: a, a certain (known to the speaker, not named)
terms.grammar: indefinite adjective; as a pronoun quīdam, quaedam, quiddam
evidence: Phaedr. 2.5.1: est ardaliōnum quaedam Rōmae nātiō
terms.comment: The “a” of a story, or of someone one has in mind: “a man I know”. See “someone”.

terms.grammar: numeral adjective; genitive ūnīus, dative ūnī
evidence: Vulg. Jo. 6.9: Est puer ūnus hīc

phrases.latin: canis per flūmen carnem cum ferret natāns
phrases.english: a dog was swimming across a river with a piece of meat
there is at Rome a tribe of busybodies

phrases.latin: Est puer ūnus hīc quī habet quīnque pānēs hordeāceōs et duōs piscēs
phrases.english: There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish
